assumptions_and_conventions: Real finite-dimensional linear model z=A theta+e with e in the declared error set E; no additional physical restriction on theta in Theorem 2.
A+ is the Moore-Penrose inverse, P_A=A A+, E_z={e in E:(I-P_A)(z-e)=0}, and Theta_lin={A+(z-e)+k:e in E_z,k in ker A}.
J is a real linear carrier and a is its real functional direction. The support is the extended-real supremum; sup over the empty set is -infinity.
Compactness of E is needed for the compact identifiable image and finite support branch, not for the existence of a feasible kernel ray.
